statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail), and r is a height-balanced binary search tree whose inorder traversal is exactly nums. Concretely: define height(Null)=0 and height(Node(v,l,rr))=1+max(height(l),height(rr)); say a tree is height-balanced if every node t=Node(v,l,rr) satisfies balanced(l), balanced(rr), and |height(l)-height(rr)| <= 1, with Null balanced. Define inorder(Null)=[] and inorder(Node(v,l,rr))=inorder(l) ++ [v] ++ inorder(rr). Say a tree is a BST if for every node t=Node(v,l,rr), every value occurring in l is strictly less than v and every value occurring in rr is strictly greater than v. Then r is height-balanced, r is a BST, and inorder(r)=nums.
